Command: Do not kindle fire on the Sabbath day
Summary: No fire may be kindled in Israel's dwellings on the Sabbath day, setting the day apart from ordinary work.
Commandment: Kindle no fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The fire ban made the Sabbath rest visible in every home: even the day's ordinary preparations stopped. Debated: some Christians keep the Sabbath day as a binding command; others see its rest fulfilled in Christ (Hebrews 4; Colossians 2:16-17). The site does not settle the question.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the Sabbath is the LORD's day of rest, kept holy in remembrance of creation and of deliverance from Egypt (Exodus 20:8-11; Deuteronomy 5:12-15).
